cards.title: What is democracy?
cards.text: Democracy means rule by the people. Citizens choose leaders by voting and can remove them at the next election.

qs.q: In a democracy, power ultimately rests with…

cards.title: Who runs an election?
cards.text: In India an independent body, the Election Commission, organises elections and makes sure they are fair.

qs.q: Why must the election body be independent?

cards.title: Why vote?
cards.text: One vote may look small, but millions of votes decide who makes the laws that shape everyday life.

options: Votes decide who makes our laws
It is optional for democracy to work

cards.title: Rights and duties
cards.text: Rights such as free speech come with duties such as respecting others and obeying the law.

qs.q: Freedom of speech comes with the duty to…

cards.title: Fundamental rights
cards.text: Fundamental rights protect everyone, such as equality, freedom and education, and courts can enforce them.

cards.title: Three arms of government
cards.text: The legislature makes laws, the executive carries them out and the judiciary settles disputes. Each checks the others.

cards.title: Checks and balances
cards.text: Dividing power among institutions stops any one of them from becoming too strong.

cards.title: Rule of law
cards.text: Rule of law means everyone, including leaders, must follow the same laws.

cards.title: Free press
cards.text: A free press informs voters and questions those in power. Without it, mistakes stay hidden.

qs.q: A free press helps democracy by…

cards.title: Majority and minority
cards.text: A healthy democracy follows the majority but also protects the rights of minorities.

qs.q: A fair democracy must also protect…

cards.title: Federalism
cards.text: In a federal country power is shared between the central government and the states.

cards.title: Local government
cards.text: Panchayats and municipalities bring decisions close to people, such as water, roads and waste.

cards.title: Peaceful protest
cards.text: Peaceful protest lets citizens voice concerns. Violence harms the cause and innocent people.

cards.title: Accountability
cards.text: Accountability means leaders must explain their decisions and face consequences for failures.

cards.title: Transparency
cards.text: When government work is open to the public, corruption has fewer places to hide.

cards.title: Right to Information
cards.text: The RTI law lets citizens ask government offices for information about how decisions and money are used.

cards.title: What is corruption?
cards.text: Corruption is misusing public power for private gain, such as bribes. It slows development and hurts the poor most.

cards.title: Fighting corruption
cards.text: Honest officials, strict laws, digital records and alert citizens all help reduce corruption.

cards.title: Role of opposition
cards.text: The opposition questions the government, offers alternatives and keeps debate alive.

cards.title: Coalition government
cards.text: When no party wins a majority, parties join together to form a coalition. It needs compromise.

cards.title: Voter apathy
cards.text: When many people do not vote, a small group decides for everyone. Informed voting strengthens democracy.

cards.title: Fake news in politics
cards.text: False stories can mislead voters. Check the source before you believe or share.

qs.q: Before sharing political news, you should…

cards.title: Public opinion
cards.text: Public opinion is what ordinary people think. Governments listen to it through votes, media and protests.

cards.title: Youth in politics
cards.text: Young people bring fresh ideas and energy. Many argue they should vote and stand for office.

qs.q: A reason for youth to join politics is…

cards.title: Why countries cooperate
cards.text: Countries trade, share science and tackle problems like pandemics together because no one can solve them alone.

cards.title: United Nations
cards.text: The UN is a global body where countries discuss peace, development and human rights.

qs.q: The UN mainly aims to promote…

cards.title: Diplomacy
cards.text: Diplomacy means solving disputes through talks instead of fighting.

cards.title: Why wars happen
cards.text: Wars often start over land, resources, power or fear. Their costs fall mostly on ordinary people.

cards.title: Refugees
cards.text: Refugees flee war or persecution. Many countries debate how to help them while managing resources.

cards.title: Sanctions
cards.text: Sanctions are penalties, like trade limits, used to pressure a country without war.

cards.title: Non-alignment and balance
cards.text: India tries to keep good ties with many countries instead of joining a single bloc. This is called strategic autonomy.

cards.title: Soft power
cards.text: Soft power is influence through culture, ideas and values, such as yoga, films and food.

cards.title: Global issues
cards.text: Major global issues are climate change, poverty, pandemics, terrorism and inequality. All need cooperation.

cards.title: Terrorism
cards.text: Terrorism uses violence to spread fear for political aims. Countries share intelligence to fight it.

cards.title: Nuclear weapons
cards.text: Nuclear weapons could end huge numbers of lives, so treaties try to limit them.

qs.q: Why do treaties limit nuclear weapons?
